content.title: About
content.content: Hot Thai sauce is a spicy Thai condiment made from chili peppers, garlic, vinegar, sugar and aromatic spices. It delivers a bright, pungent flavor with hints of sweetness and acidity, perfect for marinating, dipping, or topping seafood, chicken, beef and vegetable dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sauce is based on traditional Thai recipes passed down through generations.
It blends several chili varieties, giving it a complex level of heat.
In Thailand it is used as an all‑purpose sauce for rice, noodles and soups.
Palm sugar is often added, providing a subtle caramel note.
Hot Thai sauce is a popular “challenge” sauce on cooking shows because of its intense flavor.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Capsaicin from chilies has antioxidant properties that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports metabolism
items.content: Spicy foods can boost metabolic rate and aid calorie burning.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vinegar and lime in the recipe provide vitamin C, important for the immune system.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Garlic and spices stimulate gastric juice production, improving digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The sauce contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Spicy food
items.content: Large amounts of hot sauce may irritate the stomach in people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Allergy to spices
items.content: Ingredients such as garlic or vinegar can trigger allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Those monitoring blood sugar should consider the small amount of sugar present.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: The sauce contains salt; people with hypertension should consume it in moderation.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Hot Thai sauce can be mixed into marinades, drizzled over finished dishes, used as a dip for spring rolls, shrimp, chicken wings, or as a spicy topping for noodles and rice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce in a tightly sealed bottle in the refrigerator. Once opened, it stays good for about 3‑6 months. Discard if you notice off‑odors or mold growth.
